title: Hospices that lost Medicare billing rights: what they had been paid, and whether the State licence is still open
question: How much did Medicare pay the California hospices and home-health agencies it later revoked, and does the State still list them as open?
finding: 402 of the 479 hospices on the federal list of revoked Medicare enrolments are in California. Medicare had paid 339 of them $1,264.7 million over fiscal 2018 to 2024, $411.2 million in 2024 alone (9.5% of all Medicare hospice payments in the State). The most common reasons: abuse of billing privileges: pattern or practice (179); affiliation that poses an undue risk (140); on-site review (78). 86 of the 402 still appear in the State's listing of open licensed hospices dated 16 October 2026 (those 86 were paid $109.6 million in 2024). Hospices enrolled in Medicare in California fell from 2,212 in the 2023-04 file to 1,142 in 2026-10; 395 of the 1,481 that left are on the revoked list. 43 California home-health agencies are on the same list (paid $286.5 million over 2018 to 2024). In the six Bay Area counties: 1 (Devotion Hospice Care Inc, Hayward, revoked 2025-04-18, paid $2.5 million).
how: The federal list of revoked enrolments (July 2026) was joined to the quarterly Medicare enrolment files on the enrolment number, an exact identifier; the enrolment gives the federal certification number, which was joined to Medicare's provider payment files (hospice: fiscal 2018 to 2024; home health: calendar 2018 to 2024) and to the State's listing of open licensed facilities (16 October 2026) on the certification number and the kind of facility. Reasons are printed as the list gives them, without the regulation numbers. Bay Area rows come first, then the largest totals.
limits: A revocation ends billing privileges; it is not a finding of fraud against any person, it can be appealed, and some are reversed. "Affiliation that poses an undue risk" means the agency disclosed a tie to another party with a past problem. Payments shown were made before the revocation and may have been for real care. A State licence is a separate permission from Medicare enrolment: a hospice can hold one and serve privately paying or Medi-Cal patients, and the State listing may lag a closure. The payment files stop at 2024, so nothing here shows money after a revocation. The revoked list keeps an entry only while its re-enrolment bar runs.
